source_excerpts.text:
Fix J,tau>0 and kappa>lambda_c/3, lambda_c=2J*pi^2. Set

 lambda=lambda_*(kappa)=inf_{theta!=0}
 [(J/2)int theta'^2-kappa int rho^2]/int rho,
 theta in H^1_0(0,1),0<=theta<=pi, rho=sin^2(theta/2).

The previously audited classical sine trial gives lambda<lambda_c.
There are S=L-1 spin sites, BOTH endpoint fields, and

 Hcrit=J sum_{i=1}^{S-1}(I-sigma_i dot sigma_{i+1})
                        +J(I-Z_1)+J(I-Z_S),
 A_L=L^2 Hcrit, N=sum n_i, W=sum n_i n_{i+1},
 B_L=A_L-kappa W-lambda N, Z_L=Tr exp(-tau B_L).

Thus physical V_L=-4J-kappa/L^2 and beta=tau L^2. All spin sectors
are retained. N COMMUTES with B_L. No eigenbasis or Gibbs sampler is
supplied. The inherited contact/cube/trace modules are spelled out in
Section6; the macroscopic trial lower bound itself does not use the
matching Gamma-liminf or a full partition upper bound.

3. Exact endpoint completion and O(1/L) SCALED trial energy
----------------------------------------------------------
Put h=1/L, theta_i=theta(ih), rho_i=sin^2(theta_i/2), including the ghost
values theta_0=theta_L=rho_0=rho_L=0. Let psi_L be the product spinor
cos(theta_i/2)|0>+sin(theta_i/2)|1> on physical sites i=1,...,L-1.

The interior bond expectation is J[1-cos(theta_{i+1}-theta_i)]. Each
endpoint killing expectation is2J rho_i=J[1-cos(theta_i)]. It EXACTLY
equals the missing ghost bond, rather than merely being negligible.
For Delta theta_i=theta_{i+1}-theta_i and Delta rho_i=rho_{i+1}-rho_i,

 <Hcrit>_psi=J sum_{i=0}^{L-1}[1-cos(Delta theta_i)],
 <N>_psi=sum_{i=1}^{L-1}rho_i,
 <W>_psi=sum_{i=1}^{L-1}rho_i^2
                       -(1/2)sum_{i=0}^{L-1}(Delta rho_i)^2.    (3.1)

The contact identity follows by expanding the squared differences and
using both ghost values. It retains the exact physical contact sum
over i=1,...,L-2; no artificial boundary interaction is introduced.

Quantitative estimates, with all constants charged:
cell mean derivatives obey
int theta'^2-L sum(Delta theta_i)^2
 =sum_cells int|theta'-cellmean(theta')|^2
 <=h^2 pi^{-2}int theta''^2.
Also sum(Delta theta_i)^4<=h^3||theta'||_infinity^2||theta'||_2^2.
Using |1-cos z-z^2/2|<=z^4/24 gives

 |<A_L>_psi-L(J/2)int theta'^2|
 <=h[J int theta''^2/(2pi^2)
                  +J||theta'||_infinity^2||theta'||_2^2/24].    (3.2)

For a C^2 function f with f(0)=f(1)=0, its composite trapezoid rule is
h sum_{i=1}^{L-1}f(ih). The Peano kernel gives absolute error
<=h^2 int|f''|/8, hence |sum f_i-L int f|<=h int|f''|/8.
Apply this to rho and rho^2. Finally sum(Delta rho_i)^2<=h int rho'^2.
Therefore

 |<B_L>_psi-L E_{kappa,lambda}(theta)|<=C_theta/L,
 C_theta=J int theta''^2/(2pi^2)
      +J||theta'||_infinity^2||theta'||_2^2/24
      +kappa int|(rho^2)''|/8+(kappa/2)int rho'^2
      +|lambda|int|rho''|/8.                              (3.3)

At coexistence E(theta)=0, so the SCALED energy <B_L> is O(1/L).
There is no hidden O(1) endpoint/Euler--Maclaurin bias. This precise
estimate is stronger than the earlier point-profile recovery, which
only controlled its leading energy. No sign of the O(1/L) bias is assumed.

Bounded detunings of order1/L preserve the conclusion. If
kappa_L=kappa+zeta_L/L, lambda_L=lambda_*+eta_L/L with bounded zeta_L,
eta_L, the SAME profile has

 <B_L(kappa_L,lambda_L)>_psi
 =-zeta_L int rho^2-eta_L int rho+o(1),                 (7.1)

by(3.1)--(3.3). Its macro projected energy stays bounded, so(5.2) still
gives c sqrt L uniformly for bounded detunings. The dilute comparison
has a uniform strict gap below lambda_c, giving uniform bounded Z_lo.
If zeta_L->zeta,eta_L->eta, the lower coefficient in(5.3) is multiplied
by exp[tau(zeta int rho^2+eta int rho)]. This is a lower bound, not an
exact coexistence-weight formula.

Certifying additive errors O(1/L) in kappa and lambda is SUFFICIENT to
invoke this result's bounded-detuning robustness window. It is not a
proved necessary precision for every macroscopic-escape regime. This
certificate costs O(log L) precision bits plus the accuracy needed to
acquire lambda_*.
Computing/certifying lambda_* or the minimizer is NOT a supplied free
oracle or an efficient acquired algorithm here. If L detuning is
unbounded, the finite trial bias must be retained; these conclusions
must not automatically be exported to every moving approach to lambda_*.

For example a downward field shift lambda_L=lambda_*-a log(L)/L changes
the lower bound to order at least L^{1/2-tau a mu+o(1)}. It still diverges
when tau a mu<1/2, but supplies no matching upper or classification for
larger a. There is no claimed sharp finite-size transition width.
